purpose: Covers the lead-deletion flow: a confirmation modal (with a deletion reason) shown when deleting a single lead, and the "Deleted Leads" folder view where soft-deleted leads live for 30 days and can be restored or permanently deleted.
flowNarrative: The user initiates deletion of the lead "Olivia Martinez" from elsewhere in the module (the trigger screen is not part of this section). Screen 779:24663 shows the resulting confirmation modal over a dimmed backdrop: it names the lead and its current stage, asks for a deletion Reason via a dropdown (currently "Spam"), and warns that the lead will be permanently deleted in 30 days but remains visible to collaborators in the deleted folder. The user either cancels or confirms with the red Delete button. Screen 779:26316 is that deleted folder: a full-width "Deleted Leads" overlay (breadcrumb "Leads /") listing the soft-deleted lead in a table. An amber banner repeats the 30-day permanent-removal policy. The Olivia Martinez row is shown in a selected state (checked checkbox, lavender row highlight), which surfaces a floating selection bar at the bottom with a count of 1 and "Restore" / "Delete Forever" actions; the row itself also carries an inline "Restore" link and a red action cropped at the frame edge. "Empty Trash" in the header offers clearing the whole folder, and the X closes the view. A footer note explains deleted leads are hidden from the board and reports and that Restore returns a lead to its original status. Note: the prototype wiring spec confirms there is no screen-to-screen navigation in the file — the sequence is implied by screen numbering, not links.

purpose: Documents the two filtering mechanisms on the Leads listing: (1) the quick stage-filter dropdown on the toolbar pill that narrows the table to one pipeline stage, and (2) the full "Filters" modal with a left tab rail (Sort, Property type, Source, Assignees, Date) whose selections are applied via a shared Clear All / Apply footer.
flowNarrative: The user starts on the Leads table and clicks the stage pill in the toolbar ("All Leads (99)" with chevron), opening the stage dropdown (780:93492). The menu groups stages under ACTIVE (New, Contacted, Met, Quote Sent, Won) and INACTIVE (On Hold, Lost), each with a count of 99, plus a "Manage Stages >" link at the bottom. Choosing a stage produces the filtered view (780:94292), where the pill now reads "On Hold (2)" and the table shows exactly the two On Hold leads (Farah Ahmad, Muthu Vinay). Independently, the toolbar's filter icon-button implies opening the "Filters" modal. The modal opens on its first rail tab, Sort (779:24983), offering two radio options (Newest/Oldest at the top). The user can switch rail tabs: Property type (781:53980) shows a searchable checkbox list of 21 property types in divider-separated groups (HDB, BTO, Condo, Landed, Commercial, Others); Source (781:54190) shows a searchable checkbox list of 12 lead sources — and in this crop a small purple dot badge sits next to "Property type" in the rail, implying selections were made on that tab; Assignees (781:54363) shows a two-line avatar list of team members with checkboxes, "Dane — Owner (you)" checked; Date (781:54536) shows choice chips (Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Custom — Custom selected) with "From date" / "To date" fields, each with a calendar icon. Every modal tab shares the same footer: outlined "Clear All" and primary "Apply". Note: per design-source/context/interaction-states.md, the Figma prototype contains no screen-to-screen navigation — this sequence is carried by screen numbering, and all wired reactions are component-state changes (search focus, radios, switches, filter-row icons).

purpose: Documents the full "change stage" journey for a lead: opening the stage dropdown from the Leads listing table, then the "Move stage" modal with a per-stage right panel (New = assignees, Contacted = contact logs with Auto Fill, Met = meeting log, Quote Sent = quote attachment, Won = signed quote/contract + payment milestones), plus the lightweight On Hold and Lost dialogs.
flowNarrative: The journey starts on the Leads listing (780:86452), where clicking a row's STAGE cell opens a dropdown listing the pipeline: an ACTIVE group (New, Contacted, Met, Quote Sent, Won) and an INACTIVE group (On Hold, Lost). The remaining screens are the "Move stage" modal for lead "Olivia Martinez", one variant per target stage. (Per the interaction-states spec, no prototype links wire these screens together — the sequence is carried by frame numbering, so the dropdown-to-modal transition is implied, not wired.) 780:86258 shows the modal with current stage New: a left rail of stage radios and a right panel titled "New" with an Assignees checklist (Dane "Owner (you)" checked). Selecting Contacted (780:89011) shows "Moving to Contacted" with a "Log 1" card: "Contacted via" chips (WhatsApp/Email/SMS/Call/Others), When + Outcome fields, "Attach screenshots of your call attempts", and Notes. Its "Auto Fill" action opens a nested upload dialog (780:89277) that accepts a conversation screenshot. 781:58292 shows the log after filling/Auto Fill: WhatsApp selected, When "12/3/2025, 3:00PM", Outcome "Callback requested", a "Next step: Schedule a call" block (Date & Time "24/8/2025, 7:00PM", Preferred mode WhatsApp), and an attached screenshot thumbnail labelled Q-101. A nested "Suggested tasks" dialog (780:89545) then offers an auto-added task and a suggestion to save. "+ Add Log" produces a second log (780:89798) with Log 1 collapsed and an empty Log 2 expanded. Moving to Met (780:90106, current stage now Contacted) asks Where ("In person") and Date & Time, plus meeting documents and notes. Moving to Quote Sent starts on a From System tab with no quotes and a "Create Quote" link (780:90353); with system quotes it becomes a selectable radio list of approved quotes (780:90575). The Upload tab offers a PDF dropzone (780:90809), an uploading state (780:91042), and an uploaded state with the file row plus a "Quote amount (S$)" field (780:91365). 780:91593 is the validation failure: Contacted and Met carry red error icons in the rail and a footer error reads "Unable to move. Please update the missing stages." Moving to Won (780:91853) requires a client signed quote and signed contract (From System selections shown), a Payment milestone table (Deposit 10% / Commencement 30% / Mid-Project 30% / Completion 30%, Total row), a Project type field, and a "Save & Convert to Project" primary action; 780:91935 is the same screen with both attach sections on their Upload tabs and milestone percentages at "0 %". Finally, the inactive stages use a small centered dialog: On Hold (780:92955) asks Reason ("Property delay") and Duration ("3 months") with helper "Next follow up date will be 22 Oct '26" and "Save & Move"; Lost (780:93425) asks only Reason ("Property too far") with "Save & Move".
